title: There are no Collatz m-cycles with m ≤ 91
notes: Journal of Integer Sequences 26 (2023) Article 23.3.5. Proves every nontrivial Collatz m-cycle has m≥92, where m is the number of local minima. Valley arrangement carries cycle information beyond (K,L) parity counts; the argument is Diophantine, not spectral. Cited from docs/problems/juggler_cycle_word_functional.md. READ FROM THE PDF, 19 September 2026 (docs/problems/juggler_collatz_finance_mirror.md): Definition 4 takes the floor X_0 = 695 * 2^60; the introduction attributes the period bound K > 7.2e10 odd steps to Hercher and Puchert 2018 (hercher-2018-collatz-cycle-length); Lemma 8 is the 2-adic run congruence, k consecutive odd steps force n = -1 mod 2^k hence n >= 2^k - 1; Theorem 16 is the finance identity 2^(K+L) = product over odd n of (3 + 1/n) with T(n_i) the reciprocal sum over a run; Corollary 17 gives sum T(n_i) <= (97/54) m/X_0; Theorem 27 gives sum T(n_i) <= (3/4) K/X_0 independently of m via Lemma 26's averaging over at most three consecutive runs; Corollary 29 reaches X_0 >= 1536 * 2^60 by tracking residue classes modulo powers of two computationally. CORRECTION to the earlier sentence 'the Juggler run-type count e is the analogous valley count': Paper A's Theorem 3.31 bounds the number of even letters by a census of run forms, while Hercher bounds the number of local minima by a Diophantine argument; the Juggler m-cycle problem is open for every m, including m = 1 (J-cycle-gaps-are-mirror-images, J-collatz-walk-charge-constant).
